summary: Hunlock Creek lumberman who ran four mills and served 25 years as justice of the peace; probably John's 3rd cousin 4 times removed.
bio:
Hiram Croop was born on 15 July 1832 in Union (now Hunlock) Twp., Luzerne Co., PA, the eldest of the seven children of William Croop and Mary Sorber, and so a grandson of both John Croop and Philip Sorber. In 1854 he married Susanna Dodson, daughter of Joseph B. and Martha Dodson.

He became a lumberman on a large scale, at one time running four mills and owning 2,000 acres of timber, with a store at Croop's mills. By 1893 he owned farms of 180 and 125 acres in Hunlock Twp. and had served as justice of the peace for twenty-five years. In October 1883 he stood surety of $4,000 for Franklin Monroe, who was accused of shooting a tramp at Hunlock Creek. He is probably John's 3rd cousin 4 times removed.
sources: [R4-S1] H. C. Bradsby, History of Luzerne County (1893), pp.584 and 812-813 (Hiram and Andrew Croop biographies) (secondary) https://archive.org/details/historyofluzerne00brad

events.title: Marriage
events.description: Married Susanna, daughter of Joseph B. and Martha Dodson; five children, three living in 1893: Martha, Joseph H. (studying medicine in Philadelphia) and Fredrick W. [R4-S1]

events.title: Surety in a shooting case
events.description: When Franklin Monroe was charged with shooting a tramp at Hunlock Creek, Judge Woodward admitted him to bail on habeas corpus, and 'Hiram Croop became his surety in the sum of $4,000'. [R4-S2]
